content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "missing_justification", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quote is in the text and means what the objector says: all remaining linear terms are lumped into O(n+m). Expanding (4) at x=x_0+nc, y=y_0+me exactly gives (cn-em)^2 + 2(x_0-y_0)(cn-em) + n[2c^2-4ce+2c(x_0-y_0)] + m[2ce-2e(x_0-y_0)] + const. Since in both cases m grows proportionally to n (Case 1: m=pk, n=qk; Case 2: em=cn+O(1)), an O(n+m) remainder is Theta(n) and can dominate 4c(c-e)n, so (5) as displayed supports nothing. The claim is rescued only by the omitted regrouping 2ce\u00b7m = 2c(em) = 2c(cn-theta), which converts the m-terms into 4c^2 n plus bounded terms, yielding exactly 4c(c-e)n + O(1). The text merely asserts \"+O(1)\" in Case 2 and ignores the remainder in Case 1; this computation appears nowhere, so obligation (N)(i) is incomplete as written."}
